method: Chip **Apple M5 Max** · Metal. Harness `raw-gpu/examples/detail-live-timing.rs` (`cargo run --release -p raw-gpu --example detail-live-timing -- <RAW> [edge] [ticks]`); the files beside this row's `run.json` are its unedited stdout. Each tick is timed from `render_chain_to_f32` to GPU completion, with no readback and no host or display latency, so these numbers are engine-level and not comparable with the editor rows above. "Default" is `AdjustmentModel::default` over a Neutral scene-linear upload; "engaged" adds luminance NR 40, colour NR 50, clarity 30, texture 25, dehaze 20 and sharpening 60; "engaged + creative stage" is the engaged model over the capture decode with the creative stage in place of white balance, which is the chain the shipping hosts run. 120 warm ticks per drag. Before is `origin/main` at `3109035232` plus only this PR's timing example file (`raw-gpu/examples/detail-live-timing.rs`), so it has no resume cut; after is this branch; the two binaries ran interleaved, two rounds, on 2026-11-26.
first_late_note: First late tick after an upstream change: each of 120 iterations renders an exposure tick (a new prefix, so nothing is stored) and then a contrast tick on that prefix. With the resume cut that contrast tick runs the whole chain and also stores the image before the view transform; the tick after it resumes. It is cheaper than the exposure tick in both builds because the resident haze map is reused once the prefix stops moving, so the store's own cost is the difference between the before and after columns. An exposure, white-balance or HSL drag, whose prefix moves every tick, never stores, so it pays no copy at all.
copy_note: The store copy alone: one plane the size of the session's image, copied buffer to buffer and submitted, against an empty submit, 120 of each interleaved.
caveat: > **Recording conditions:** other agents were compiling on the same Mac throughout, at the load averages above, so absolute times are inflated and noisy; compare before and after within a row and round.
